subject: Harmonizing renewal term + laddered capacity + top-up path
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Ellen Park <ellen@datascope.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 22 Mar 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal planning — harmonizing term and laddered capacity

Hi Ellen,

Thanks again for the time last week — appreciate the walkthrough of your Q3/Q4 roadmap. As discussed, we put together a proposed renewal structure that aligns contract term, predictable commit laddering, and a top-up mechanism for occasional bursts. I attached a draft term sheet for your procurement review (DS-term-sheet-v3.pdf) and your usage forecast file for reference.

High level proposal:
- 3-year agreement with annual laddered commits (year 1: 250k tokens/mo equivalent; year 2: 375k; year 3: 550k)
- Auto-renew opt-out notice window of 60 days
- Top-up credits purchased ad hoc with fixed per-unit price and 30-day settlement
- Early burst capacity: ability to request temporary burst nodes (up to 2x month commit) with 72-hour lead time

Next steps if this looks directionally right:
1) Procurement review of attached term sheet and any required legal language.
2) Confirm whether DataScope needs co-terminus dates across multiple lines of business (you mentioned a separate analytics BU).
3) If OK, I can open a canary renewal in HubSpot and schedule a short commercial call with finance to finalize the discount ladder.

Appreciate your thoughts — if you'd like, we can propose two variants (frontloaded credits vs. smoothed ladder) for comparison.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0182

Attachment: DS-term-sheet-v3.pdf (term sheet draft, 6 pages)
Attachment: datascope-usage-forecast-q2-q4.xlsx (forecast workbook)

From: Ellen Park <ellen@datascope.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@datascope.ai
Date: Thu, 23 Mar 2028 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal planning — harmonizing term and laddered capacity

Kim — thanks for the quick turnaround and the draft. High-level this matches what our CFO would prefer (multi-year with predictable ramp). A few procurement asks before we hand to legal: 

- Can you confirm whether the top-up per-unit price is fixed for the full term or resets annually?
- We need a clause for data residency guarantees tied to our EU customers (we may isolate some workloads).
- Curious how the early burst request impacts SLOs — will it be best-effort or SLA-backed?

I'll share the draft with procurement/legal and expect an initial redline within two business days. We also want two pricing scenarios: (A) 3-yr ladder as proposed with a 12% average discount vs list and (B) 2-yr with higher frontloaded credits and a 9% average.

Can you loop in finance for scenario modeling?

—Ellen
Ellen Park
Head of Platform, DataScope.ai
ellen@datascope.ai

Thanks — ran the numbers and attached a model (internal only). Summary:

Scenario A (3yr ladder, 12% avg):
- Year 1 ARR: $1.8M (baseline commit 250k/mo)
- Year 2 ARR: $2.7M (375k/mo)
- Year 3 ARR: $4.0M (550k/mo)
- Effective blended per-token price: $0.00075
- Notes: amortize onboarding credit over first 6 months reduces Y1 recognized revenue slightly

Scenario B (2yr frontload, 9% avg):
- Year 1 ARR (frontloaded credits): $2.6M
- Year 2 ARR: $2.9M
- Effective blended per-token price: $0.00083

Recommendation: Scenario A gives stronger long-term ARR and predictable upsell runway; Scenario B offers better near-term cash but lower 3-yr lift.

I'll attach the model: datascope-renewal-model-rishi.xlsx (internal).

Rishi
Director, Commercial Finance

Kim & team — appreciate the quick turnaround and the two scenarios. Procurement attached a short redline PDF (procurement-redline-v1.pdf) — I'll upload to your Drive link but key ask is:

- Top-up price must be fixed for at least the first 12 months of the term.
- EU residency carve-out: we need a statement that EU workloads can be constrained to EU regions at no additional per-token premium, pending capacity planning.
- Burst SLA: acceptable if best-effort but with credit-based remediation if sustained below 95th percentile for more than 48 hours.

Ellen

Ellen — thanks for the procurement feedback and redline summary. We can commit to: 

1) Fixed top-up price for the first 12 months (we'll include renewal reset language for subsequent years with advance notice).
2) EU residency carve-out: we will guarantee region-constrained routing for EU-designated workloads at no incremental per-token premium, subject to a 45-day capacity alignment window.
3) Burst SLA: we propose best-effort burst fulfillment plus a credits-based remediation if the 48-hour sustained performance drop condition is met (we'll propose specific credit calculations in the term sheet).

Attached is an updated term sheet with tracked changes (DS-term-sheet-v4.pdf). For next steps, Ellen: if the updated sheet is acceptable, can procurement sign off on the non-substantive commercial points and pass legal redlines by EOD Friday 7 Apr? We'll prepare a final pricing addendum (Scenario A and B) and a short implementation SOW for the first 90 days.

Looping Marissa to prep the TCO one-pager and Priyom to add the burst operational runbook. Rishi — please finalize the HubSpot deal with both scenario pricecards and set the renewal target close date to 2028-04-20.

Best,
Kim
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
